title: Chicken Goujons
subtitle: Strips of chicken breast in a crisp golden breadcrumb coating
excerpt: Chicken breast strips coated in seasoned breadcrumbs and shallow-fried or oven-baked until golden. A pub-menu staple and family favourite that makes a far better version than anything from the freezer.
sourceNotes: Goujons (the French term for fried strips of fish or meat) became a fixture on British pub menus from the 1980s onwards, usually made with chicken breast. The dish is closely related to the American chicken tender but uses a finer breadcrumb coating rather than a thick batter. Recipe developed from first principles.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze breaded (uncooked) goujons on a tray. Once solid, transfer to a bag. Cook from frozen at 200 degrees C for 25 to 30 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Double or triple easily. Bread in batches and refrigerate before cooking.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The breaded goujons can be refrigerated for up to 4 hours before cooking. The crust sets firmer when chilled.

content.text: Chicken goujons are strips of chicken breast in seasoned breadcrumbs, baked or shallow-fried until the coating is golden and the chicken is cooked through. The key is the three-stage breading: flour, egg, then crumbs. Each layer serves a specific role and all three are needed. Chilling the breaded pieces before cooking helps the coating stay on.

items.prepNote: cut into strips about 1 cm thick and 8 cm long
fine dried, or panko for a lighter crust

content.text: Cut {{chicken-breast}} of chicken breast into strips. Set up three shallow bowls: one with {{plain-flour}} of flour seasoned with salt and pepper, one with {{eggs}} beaten eggs, one with {{breadcrumbs-dried}} of breadcrumbs mixed with {{smoked-paprika}} of smoked paprika and garlic powder if using.
Pass each strip through flour (shake off excess), then egg (let excess drip off), then breadcrumbs (press to coat). Lay on a clean tray.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes. This helps the coating adhere during cooking.
Heat the oven to 200 degrees C. Drizzle a baking tray with {{sunflower-oil}} of oil and heat in the oven for 5 minutes. Lay the goujons on the hot tray in a single layer.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, turning once halfway, until golden and cooked through. Cut the thickest one open to check: the inside should be white with no pink.

rows.cause: Flour stage skipped, or egg not drained before crumbing
rows.fix: All three stages are essential. Shake off the excess flour and let the excess egg drip before rolling in crumbs.

rows.cause: Oven not hot enough, or tray not preheated
rows.fix: Preheat the oiled tray in the oven. The sizzling hot surface crisps the underside as soon as the goujons go on.

rows.cause: Overcooked, or strips cut too thin
rows.fix: Cut strips at least 1 cm thick. 18 to 20 minutes at 200 degrees C is enough for strips of this size.

rows.symptom: Coating is thick and bready rather than light
rows.fix: Press the crumbs on firmly but do not pile them up. One even layer is enough.

content.text: Chicken goujons appeared on British pub menus in the 1980s and quickly became one of the most popular items in casual dining. They sit between the formal breadcrumbed escalope and the frozen chicken nugget. They work well in both settings: in a pub basket with garlic mayo, or at home as a Friday-night dinner for children and adults. The name comes from the French goujon, a small fried fish.
